Navin's rules for this task (follow every one):
[G-01] Everything taught comes from the book. Knowledge from outside the book is allowed only to explain the book better; it is marked as outside, standard textbook-level and correct. Never invent facts, numbers, names or quotations.
[G-02] Work like the best teacher of these learners and this exam, not like a summariser. Depth beats brevity: nothing teachable on the page is skipped or compressed away, and every explanation makes a student understand, not just remember. Depth means understanding, not length: lesson narration keeps S2-01's time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-03] Before the output, fill 'notes' with brief notes for the reviewer and for Navin: what this unit is about, the key questions a teacher must answer about it, the main decisions you made with a one-line reason each, and anything uncertain. Keep the notes short; they explain the work, they are not the work.
[G-04] Learner-facing language follows the course setting. For the first course (UPSC / State PCS) it is Hinglish: natural Hindi sentence flow, English technical terms, the way Navin teaches.
[G-05] Never drop or compress away what the book teaches to fit a length. If a unit of work is too large, it is split by BIE into smaller units; within a unit, the book's content is complete. Lesson narration has a time target (S2-01), met by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-06] BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher (Navin, 24 October 2026). The book is the base; BIE carries its text, easy or hard, into the learner's mind. Never just read the line out: every book line is opened (what its words mean, why it is so, where it is seen, what follows), at the depth of the level profile.
[G-07] Two layers, like a film (Navin, 24 October 2026). The writer layer (understanding, plan, script) decides what is said and how deep, following the level profile and the book's own level. The presentation layer (director, video blocks, render) is the same skilled quality for every learner, from class 6 to postgraduate; only the detail shown follows the level, never the craft.
[S2-01] Plan the chapter's videos from the chapter map: first one short 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video (5-8 minutes) that teaches the chapter's prerequisites, then the topic videos in teaching order. Narration is 6-8 minutes per book page (Navin, 23 October 2026; the 14-page tissue chapter about 85-110 minutes of topic videos, plus the prerequisite video): each topic video gets the share of the pages its items come from, and a very dense page may go up to 25% over when the plan says why. Understanding (Section 1) and the chapter map have no time limit.
[S2-02] Write a spoken teacher script in beats with a natural teacher flow. Stories and analogies only where they genuinely help that topic. Every item the book teaches is taught and every teacher question answered from the book is answered; questions answered from outside the book are used only where they help and the time allows. Cut repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[S2-03] Prerequisites are only what this chapter directly needs, never a prerequisite of a prerequisite. They are taught, not named, in the chapter's 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video, each with a simple explanation and an example; a topic video may remind of them in at most 2 beats.
[S2-04] Spoken Hinglish the way Navin teaches, in mixed script (Navin, 21 and 23 October 2026): Hindi words in Devanagari, English words, above all the book's technical terms, in Roman exactly as the book spells them, as in 'आज हम tissue के बारे में पढ़ेंगे'; a genuinely difficult Hindi word (formal, literary or technical; not in BIE's everyday word list rulebook/simple_hindi.json) gets its English word in brackets right after it, as in 'सतह (surface)'; the screen and subtitles show the bracket and the voice says 'सतह, यानी surface'. Never a bracket after an everyday word or inside an idiom or a fixed phrase ('आम तौर पर', not 'आम तौर (usually) पर'; 'नहीं के बराबर', not 'नहीं के बराबर (equal to)'). Never an English term in Devanagari or a Hindi word in Roman. Numbers as digits; short spoken sentences addressed to one student; questions to the student and natural pauses; no reading out of lists.
[S2-05] Every beat states which chapter-map items it covers and which teacher questions it answers, and those claims must be true: the beat really explains that item and really answers that question.
[S2-06] Teach every part of a video through the universal frame (what the process is, how it works, when and in what order, under which conditions, in what atmosphere) and through the teaching pattern of its content type, step by step in the pattern's order; every item on the task card is really taught, none only named.
[S2-07] Open every book line in the script, never read it out (Navin, 24 October 2026). A new topic opens with a question about something the learner can see, then the name. After any book line the beat carries at least one of: the term's plain meaning with 'yaani' and an everyday image, a why step from a need, an example or the place. Speak complete sentences, not clipped notes. A classification is taught as a family: the overview tree, then every member in the same slots (layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence), then the members compared and a memory trick. A pattern step may be skipped only with a stated reason; one recap per part and one closing recap.
[S2-08] Apply first, name after (Navin, 27 October 2026): in an economics script a concept's real-world example runs BEFORE the beat that names the term: the example beats carry the example's numbers (₹50 → ₹65, buyers 2 → 12 → 3) and walk the mechanism step by step; then the term ('isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain'), then the book's definition, then one line on where the learner meets it in real life. The example is the one Section 1 chose for the item (its place, actors, goods, numbers), economically correct and at the learner's level.
[W-01] The narration never points at the book: no 'book के अनुसार', 'किताब कहती है', 'book says', 'page पर', 'textbook', 'NCERT' or any wording of that family (the list in this file, 'wording'). BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):
- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the result first (what it makes). 2) inputs and the place. 3) each step with its cause and its condition. 4) what breaks when a step fails. 5) the whole run once more at speed. 6) recap as a flow.
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the whole in context. 2) zoom into each part in a fixed path (outside to inside). 3) function of each part tied to its shape. 4) how the parts work together. 5) labelled recap.
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the overview tree first: the basis of division and every member named. 2) every member in the same slots: layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence. 3) the members compared side by side, the most confused pair named directly. 4) a memory trick for the family.
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what is common. 2) criteria one at a time, both sides together. 3) the reason behind each difference. 4) the most confused pair named directly. 5) difference table as recap.
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the period and its atmosphere. 2) events in order with their causes. 3) the people and their choices. 4) the turning point. 5) what changed after. 6) timeline recap.
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the effect students can see. 2) the cause. 3) each link of the chain with its mechanism. 4) the evidence. 5) the exception or limit. 6) the chain as recap.
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the fact in one line. 2) the number shown to scale against something familiar. 3) where it comes from (book or outside, dated). 4) what it changes or proves. 5) a formula built term by term when there is one.
- figure · Figure: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only). Required questions: what (kya), which (kaun). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what the figure is and why it is here. 2) a reading path across it (labels in order). 3) the one thing to remember from it. 4) link back to the text it explains.
- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) a concrete example first. 2) the book's definition word by word. 3) a non-example that tests the boundary. 4) where the term is used next in the chapter.

How BIE talks to you: every request is a task card (JSON) followed by its source. The card names the unit, its parts with their content type and required questions, the ids of the rules above that apply, the output, the ids you must cover and the context. The card is BIE's instruction; the source is the material.
For a write_script card:
- card.parts are this video's parts: each has item ids, one content type and the questions it must answer. The source gives every item's
  full content and its teacher questions with ids ("p003-i4#q2") and answers from BIE's chapter map; teach from them.
- card.coverage.must_cover lists every item this video must teach: each must be in covers_item_ids of a beat that really explains it.
  may_skip lists items you may leave out (not teachable). card.context.map_slice shows the related concepts for context only.
How to fill the JSON:
- notes: brief notes for the reviewer: what this video is about, the key questions it must answer, your main decisions (order,
  hook, analogy, where prerequisites are taught) with a reason each, what is uncertain.
- title: the video title in the learner language.
- parts: one entry per card part, with the universal frame of that part (S3-01), each in one or two lines of clear English for BIE:
  process (what happens or what the thing does), how (how it works or happens), when (when, in what order, under which timing),
  conditions (what must be true for it, or what changes it), atmosphere (the setting and situation a student should picture). Write
  "n/a: " and the reason only where a question truly does not apply to that part. skipped_steps = the teaching-pattern steps of this
  part you leave out because there is nothing real to say for them, each with the reason ([] when every step is done); at most half
  of a pattern, never a step that has something real; BIE's code records the reason.
- beats: the whole video in order. beat_id "b1", "b2" ...; part_id = the card part this beat teaches ("" for the opening hook, a
  prerequisite taught first, a transition or the final recap); step = the number of the teaching-pattern step of that part's content type
  that this beat performs (see the content types above; 0 when part_id is "" and for an exam-question part, whose type is "none");
  the steps of a part's pattern appear in order, except the ones skipped with a reason; a classification part follows the family
  pattern: the overview tree first, then every member in the same slots (layer and shape → why it is named so → its special feature
  → its function with its cause → where it is found, by a zoom from the organ → its consequence), then the comparison, then a memory
  trick; one recap per part and one closing recap for the video, never two recaps of the same thing;
  purpose (hook, prerequisite, explain, example, analogy, story, compare, process_walkthrough, misconception, exam_tip,
  question_to_student, recap, transition); say = the exact spoken words, one to four complete spoken sentences in Navin's Hinglish
  (S2-04), the way a teacher speaks to one student, never clipped note-style lines ("Irregular walls. Kaisi? Irregular." is a teacher's
  beat; "Location: kidney tubules, glandular ducts." is a note):
  mixed script: Hindi words in Devanagari, English words (above all the book's technical terms, spelled as the book spells them) in
  Roman, as in "आज हम tissue के बारे में पढ़ेंगे"; brackets only after a genuinely difficult Hindi word (see "Brackets" below; the
  screen shows the bracket and the voice says "सतह, यानी surface"); never write an English term in Devanagari or a Hindi word in Roman;
  numbers as digits; addressed to one student; covers_item_ids = the item ids this beat really explains; answers = the teacher question
  ids this beat really answers; on_screen = what the student should see while hearing it (for the director); basis = book, outside or
  mixed.
Opening the book (S2-07; BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher, never a reader of the line): every new
topic (every concept and every prerequisite) opens with a question about something the learner can see, then the name. After any
book line, the beat carries at least one of: the term opened ("yaani" + its plain meaning + one everyday image), the why from a need or
a problem, or an example or place by a zoom from the organ. The source gives every item's unpack from Section 1 (its terms, why chain,
example, consequence, visual verb) and the locked explanations: speak them, in your own teacher's words, at the depth of the level
profile below. BIE's code sends back a beat whose English words are the book's and that opens nothing ("dohraav pakad"), a clipped
sentence without a verb, a topic that opens without a question, and a second recap of the same thing.
Real-world application (S2-08; Navin, 27 October 2026: "economic concepts ko real world mein apply karke samjhao"): for an economics
definition, cause_effect or process item the source gives the real_world_example Section 1 chose (place, actors, goods, numbers before
→ after, the steps with their mechanism links, the naming sentence, the real-life link). Run that example FIRST, in beats that cover
the item and carry its numbers as digits ("dukaan mein chini ke 3 packet, ₹50 ka ek; kal 2 khareedar, aaj 12"), walking the mechanism
step by step (purpose story or example); only then the beat that names the term ("isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain"), then
the book's definition, then the real-life link. The opening question of such a topic asks about the situation, not the term. BIE's
code sends back a script whose naming beat comes before the example beats, or whose example beats carry none of the numbers.
Time (S2-01): the source gives this video's narration time; BIE's code counts the spoken words (130 a minute) and the script must stay
within it. Win the time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content: every item in must_cover is taught and every
teacher question whose basis is "book" is answered; questions answered from outside the book are used only where they help and the
time allows.
Prerequisites (S2-03): in a topic video they were already taught in the prerequisite video; remind of one in at most 2 beats (purpose
"prerequisite"). In the prerequisite video (card parts "pre1", "pre2" ...) teach each prerequisite simply, with an everyday example, in
the order given: part_id = the prerequisite id, step 0, covers_item_ids = the prerequisite ids the beat teaches, answers [].
A beat introduces at most a few new items: BIE's code measures the load of every beat (0.4 per new item plus 1 per 50 spoken words, at
most 1.8), so a beat holds at most about 70 spoken words with one new item, 50 with two and 30 with three; split longer beats. Reply
with the JSON object only.

Level profile: UPSC / State PCS (level_profiles.json; learners: UPSC and State PCS aspirants, often from arts backgrounds, who need understanding more than technical vocabulary).
- Terms: fewer technical terms: only the ones the exam asks, each opened with its plain meaning and an everyday image; a term the exam never asks is explained in words, not named.
- Why: 2 step(s); a two-step why from a need the learner can feel, then its link to daily life, health or governance.
- Where found: the main places, each linked to something the learner already knows (a disease, a food, a news item).
- Exam beats: the PYQ pattern: how this fact has been asked (statement combinations, 'which is correct', odd one out) and the wording that traps.
- Links: daily life, health, the news and earlier chapters of the same paper.

How real teachers open a book line (teacher example bank 2026-10-27.1; use these ways, in your own words):
- Open with a question on something visible (every new topic and every new family member): Skin aur stomach, kidney ke upar ek outer layer hai ki nahi? Yeh kis se bani hai? — phir naam: epithelial tissue.
- One everyday image per shape or function (every term that names a shape, a layer or a job): Chaadar bichhi ho to bistar bacha rehta hai = protective sheet. Cube wala game, har side barabar = cuboidal. Building ka pillar = columnar. Farsh ki tiles = squamous, isliye tessellated bhi kehte hain.
- The word root where it helps (a term whose parts carry its meaning): Epi yaani upar; epithelium yaani upar ki parat. Slender yaani long aur narrow.
- Why starts from a need (every why step): Pet mein HCl banta hai, isliye andar ek lining chahiye jo khud na jale. Cells bahar ki taraf hain, tootne ka chance zyada, isliye regeneration zyada.
- Contrast with the neighbour (members of one family, and what the exam confuses): Simple epithelium ka kaam protection nahi, woh compound ka hai. Zyada layers = pathogen andar nahi aata.
- Ask and repeat the key word (the one word the learner must keep): Irregular walls. Kaisi? Irregular.
- Exam memory beats by level (after the understanding, by the level profile): Yaad rakhna: brush border PCT mein. Doosre naam: pavement, tessellated. M2B = muscle to bone = tendon, B2B = bone to bone = ligament.
- Link to something already known (a new place or a new structure): Peritoneum, jaise lungs ke aas-paas pleura aur heart ke aas-paas pericardium: wahi kaam, pet ke andar.
- Meaning with two or three real examples (an abstract word in the book): Sensory perception yaani pehchanna: thanda lagna, dard hona, pressure mehsoos karna.
- Open the book's adjective (Navin's example) (a book line names a kind of surface, job or place without saying what it is): Book: 'epithelium absorptive aur secretive surfaces par milta hai'. Teacher: absorptive surface yaani jahan cheezein andar li jaati hain, jaise aant khane ke poshak tatva sokhti hai; secretive yaani jahan cells kuch bana kar bahar chhodte hain, jaise glands enzyme ya juice. Aur epithelium wahan kyon? Kyunki ek patli, lagi hui parat hi cheezon ko paar jaane de sakti hai aur bana kar chhod sakti hai.
- Apply it in the real world first, then name it (Navin's sugar shop) (every economics concept (a definition, a cause-and-effect chain, a process): the example runs before the term is named): Ek kirana shop mein chini ke 3 packet hain, ₹50 ka ek. Kal 2 khareedar aaye the, aaj 12 aa gaye; sab ko chini chahiye par packet 3 hi hain. Dukandar daam ₹65 kar deta hai; ab sirf 3 log kharid paate hain, baaki 9 khaali haath. Zyada log, utna hi maal, isliye daam upar. Isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain. Phir book ki definition. Phir: yahi aap Diwali se pehle sabzi mandi mein dekhte hain.

Brackets (word list 2026-10-27.2): use everyday spoken Hindi freely, without brackets (मुख्य, वापस, बराबर, आसपास, इस्तेमाल, करके, जिससे ...). Only a genuinely difficult Hindi word (formal, literary or technical) gets its English word in brackets right after it, for example "सतह (surface)", "घर्षण (friction)", "सघन (dense)"; better still, use the book's English term or a simpler Hindi word. Never put a bracket inside an idiom or a fixed phrase: "आम तौर पर", not "आम तौर (usually) पर"; "नहीं के बराबर", not "नहीं के बराबर (equal to)". BIE's code removes a bracket after an everyday word and asks for one only after a Hindi word it does not know as everyday.

Video v4: Paper money, fiat money और legal tender का फर्क
Goal: Learner gold-backed paper के milestones, fiat money के meaning और currency examples समझेगा; legal tender, commemorative coins, acceptance limits और payment instruments की boundaries अलग कर सकेगा।
Opening hook: एक note का material सस्ता है, फिर भी उससे सामान मिलता है—क्या वजह केवल उसके पीछे रखा gold है?
Story or analogy: पहले redeemable paper claim और material से अलग monetary value की situations आएँगी। फिर historical sequence, fiat definition और legal acceptance की अलग comparison होगी। Coin denomination और कुल payment limit को अलग पढ़ेंगे।
Planned minutes: 10
Narration time (S2-01): 8.5-11.4 minutes, about 1105-1482 spoken words (BIE counts 130 words a minute)
Prerequisites already taught in the prerequisite video (remind of one in at most 2 beats): Purchases, prices, debts and payments due later; Bank balances, deposits, loans and interest; Denominations, monetary arithmetic, percentages and minimum–maximum limits; Purchasing power, inflation, scarcity and liquidity; Central bank, commercial bank, government treasury and bank-to-bank settlement; Foreign currencies, exchange rates, reserves and demand–supply changes; Chronological reading: BCE/CE, centuries, dynasties and law versus implementation dates; Digital instructions, identity authentication, ledgers and payment interfaces

beats.say: क्या हर legal tender fiat ही होगा? सामान्य जोड़ ऐसा है, लेकिन universal ‘must’ गलत होगा; Bitcoin exception इसे तोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Fiat: value basis; legal tender: legal status

beats.say: याद में बना हर coin payment में चलेगा? Commemorative coins fiat issues हैं, लेकिन legal tender हो भी सकते हैं, नहीं भी; अधिकांश होने का मतलब सभी नहीं। Metal और collector value भी अलग रह सकती हैं।
beats.on_screen: Commemorative purpose ≠ automatic legal-tender status

beats.say: Pack वाला खास coin खर्च क्यों नहीं होता? Government Mint collector commemorative coins proof या UNC sets में बेचती है। Proof खास finish, UNC यानी Uncirculated; condition बचाने के लिए daily payments कम होते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Government Mint proof / UNC sets → collection rather than change drawer

beats.say: ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10, ₹20 coins की कुल limit ₹1,000 है, जैसे 50 coins ₹20 के। 50 paise का ढेर सिर्फ ₹10 तक; नीचे वाले coins payment money नहीं रहे।
beats.on_screen: Denomination groups → aggregate limits; ₹20 × 50 = ₹1,000

beats.say: 50 coins × ₹20 = ₹1,000; 1,000 coins की छूट नहीं। 50 paise के 20 coins = ₹10; denomination और total limit अलग हैं।
4 पुराने 25 paise coins से ₹1 bill चुकाएँ, दुकानदार मना करे तो ₹1 बाकी। Valid ₹1 coin दें तो ₹0; पुराने coins का legal-tender status हटना demonetization है।
beats.on_screen: Rejected old coins: ₹1 → ₹1; valid coin: ₹1 → ₹0

beats.say: Coinage Act, 2011 वाले limits में 50 paise अलग है; डिब्बे का 25 paise उसमें नहीं आता। Commemorative coins के लिए ‘most’ यानी सभी नहीं; इससे कोई गिनती नहीं मिलती।
beats.on_screen: 50 paise has its own limit; 25 paise is below that denomination; 'most' supplies no count

beats.say: Limit पार करना status खोना नहीं; collector price legal status लौटाती नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Excess amount ≠ demonetization

beats.say: Denomination × count निकालिए; फिर total limit और status जाँचिए।
beats.on_screen: Total = denomination × count → ceiling + status

beats.say: Phone पर Bitcoin payment दिखे तो government-issued money है? नहीं; El-Salvador का example issuance और legal status अलग करता है।
beats.on_screen: Network issuance ≠ government issuance

beats.say: 2024 तक का account Bitcoin को non-fiat legal-tender exception दिखाता है। Mining network rules से होती है; price demand-supply से, government के fixed-value promise से नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Dated account: non-fiat + legal recognition; network rules and market price

beats.say: 2025 reforms के बाद practical compulsory acceptance हटी; यानी दोनों राज़ी हों तो payment कर सकते हैं, लेना ज़रूरी नहीं। Ownership और voluntary use legal हैं—ban नहीं।
beats.on_screen: 2025 practical account: optional payment remains; compulsion removed

beats.say: Recognition से network issuance सरकारी नहीं बनती; यह पूरा statutory account भी नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Changed legal recognition ≠ changed issuer

beats.say: अलग पूछिए: issuer कौन, ownership legal, acceptance voluntary या compulsory?
beats.on_screen: Issuer | ownership | acceptance

beats.say: ₹100 silver commemorative coin पर collector कई हज़ार क्यों दे? वही coin payment और collection में अलग role निभाता है।
beats.on_screen: One coin: payment versus collector sale

beats.say: Payment में ₹100; collector sale में कई हज़ार संभव। Face value और market price अलग हैं।
beats.on_screen: ₹100 payment value | several-thousand collector price

beats.say: Silver, condition और collectability premium दिलाते हैं, denomination नहीं बदलते।
beats.on_screen: Collector premium ≠ new denomination

beats.say: Collector price debt-settlement amount या compulsory coin-payment limit नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Market price ≠ debt discharged ≠ tender ceiling

beats.say: Payment में denomination, collection में agreed price याद रखिए।
beats.on_screen: Payment: denomination | collection: agreed price

beats.say: ₹1,000 fees का cheque currency बन गया? Clearing हो तो student deposit ₹2,000 से ₹1,000, college ₹0 से ₹1,000। Funds कम हों तो transfer नहीं, fees बाकी।
beats.on_screen: Successful cheque clearing transfers existing deposits; failed clearing leaves fees due

beats.say: Alternative credit-card route में issuer arrangement से college को settlement मिलता है; charges छोड़कर student का card debt ₹0 से ₹1,000। यहाँ existing deposit का instruction नहीं, credit इस्तेमाल हुआ।
beats.on_screen: Alternative card route: student debt ₹0 → ₹1,000

beats.say: ये payment instruments हैं: cheque bank को instruction, card credit तक पहुँच। Accepted payment method होने से वे खुद fiat currency या legal tender नहीं बनते; fiat value का आधार है, legal tender कानूनी status।
beats.on_screen: Instrument ≠ currency; acceptance ≠ legal-tender status

beats.say: आखिरी trick: backing पूछे तो gold claim, value पूछे तो authority-trust, legal tender पूछे तो recognition और limits। Collector premium और payment instrument को इनसे अलग रखिए; आगे समझेंगे gold link टूटने पर भी dollar की माँग क्यों रही।
beats.on_screen: Backing | value basis | legal status | market price | payment method

beats.say: ₹100 note का कागज़ सस्ता है, फिर भी चावल मिलते हैं—क्या पीछे gold रखा होना ज़रूरी है? और payment में कोई चीज़ ले ली जाए, तो क्या वह legal tender बन जाती है?
beats.on_screen: ₹100 note → rice; gold backing? Legal status?

beats.say: एक hypothetical पुराने bank में note 1 gram gold का claim है। लौटाने पर notes 1 से 0, gold 0 से 1 gram; आज का rupee ऐसा नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Historical illustration: 1 note → 1 gram gold

beats.say: यह gold-backed paper currency है: माँगने पर तय gold मिले। Intrinsic value यानी material की कीमत; यहाँ value paper से नहीं, redemption promise से है, जैसे सामान की receipt।
beats.on_screen: Paper material ≠ redeemable gold claim

beats.say: सिर्फ bank का gold रखना काफी नहीं; note लौटाने पर gold मिलना चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Gold assets alone ≠ redeemability

beats.say: आधार fixed gold claim था, कागज़ नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Gold claim supports paper value

beats.say: 10 grams के सामने 10 notes, हर note का claim 1 gram। इस fully backed उदाहरण में 11 notes के लिए 11 grams चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: 10 notes : 10 g → 11 notes : 11 g

beats.say: यही gold-backing constraint है; gold reserves यानी claims पूरे करने का stock।
beats.on_screen: Reserves support redemption claims

beats.say: Central bank reserves रखता, notes जारी करता, माँग पर fixed gold देता। इसलिए और notes के लिए backing चाहिए; redemption in principle था, हर जगह unrestricted नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Reserves → issue → redemption; in principle

beats.say: Claims चुकाने की क्षमता घटे, तो भरोसा टूटे और लोग gold माँगें।
beats.on_screen: Unmeetable claims → redemption pressure

beats.say: हर note पर 1 gram सिर्फ उदाहरण है, historical reserve ratio नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Illustration, not a historical reserve ratio

beats.say: Gold claim, फिर reserves की ज़रूरत, इसलिए issue पर रोक।
beats.on_screen: Claim → reserves → constrained issue

beats.say: सामान की जगह receipt चले तो? इतिहास में paper claims, सरकारी issue और acceptance rules अलग milestones बने।
beats.on_screen: Paper claim → state issue → acceptance rules

beats.say: 7th century में Tang receipts कहीं रखी value का लिखा claim देती थीं। 1023 में Song state notes आए; यानी notes सरकारी authority जारी करती थी।
beats.on_screen: 7th c. Tang receipts → 1023 Song state notes

beats.say: 1275, Yuan: compulsory यानी नियम से acceptance। 1661, Sweden के first banknotes; दुनिया के पहले नहीं—Chinese developments पहले हैं।
beats.on_screen: 1275 Yuan: compulsory → 1661 Sweden: banknotes

beats.say: 1816, Britain: Gold Standard, यानी money unit का तय gold से रिश्ता। 1944, Bretton Woods: dollar-gold link; यह official arrangement था, हर घर के लिए gold counter नहीं।
beats.on_screen: 1816 Britain: Gold Standard → 1944: dollar–gold link

beats.say: 1971 turning point: gold redemption खत्म; दोनों sequences का modern fiat endpoint यही है।
beats.on_screen: Both sequences → 1971: no gold redemption

beats.say: अब gold promise की जगह authority और trust से value समझेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Gold promise → authority and trust

beats.say: क्रम है: Chinese claims, Sweden notes, Britain gold anchor, dollar-gold link, फिर 1971 break।
beats.on_screen: Full dated timeline

beats.say: दुकानदार ₹100 note लेकर चावल क्यों दे? खरीदने पर आपकी cash ₹100 से ₹0, उसकी receipt ₹0 से ₹100; भरोसा है, आगे वही note चलेगा।
beats.on_screen: Buyer ₹100 → ₹0; seller ₹0 → ₹100 → next purchase

beats.say: यह fiat money है: value government authority और public trust से, material से नहीं। यानी आज मिला note कल groceries दिलाएगा।
beats.on_screen: Authority + continued acceptance, not material value

beats.say: Gold-backed paper का आधार redemption था; इसलिए हर paper note fiat नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Paper form ≠ fiat basis

beats.say: Fiat का आधार authority-trust; अगला सवाल, control कैसे?
beats.on_screen: Fiat value → governance question

beats.say: Press से note निकलना और पैसा जारी होना क्या एक काम है? Fiat paper या digital numbers हो सकता है; face value gold-silver से नहीं बँधी, government authority, central-bank control और public trust से जुड़ी है।
beats.on_screen: Material value; commodity backing; authority; trust

beats.say: और issue कर सकते हैं, मगर monetary policy control करती है। Printing notes बनाती है; authorised issuance circulation में लाता है। पुराने notes बदलना कुल पैसा बढ़ाना नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Printing ≠ issuance; replacement need not increase currency

beats.say: RBI banknotes जारी करता है; ₹1 note और coins government, coins distribution RBI करता है। Policy rates और liquidity से borrowing महँगी-सस्ती होती है; spending और prices तक असर समय लेता है।
beats.on_screen: Issuer distinctions; policy → borrowing → spending → prices

beats.say: Foreign price tags में codes क्यों देखें? $ वाला United States Dollar, USD, सबसे widely held और traded fiat currency है। € यानी Euro, EUR, कई EU देशों की shared currency है।
beats.on_screen: $ USD: United States Dollar; € EUR: Euro

beats.say: ¥ दिखे तो Japan या China? JPY यानी Japanese Yen, stability और global currency markets में अहम भूमिका के लिए जाना जाता है; CNY यानी Chinese Yuan Renminbi, trade और international reserves में बढ़ती भूमिका वाला पैसा।
beats.on_screen: ¥ JPY ≠ ¥ CNY

beats.say: £ वाली currency British Pound Sterling, GBP है। इसकी history 8th century तक जाती है; लेकिन currency का पुराना होना लगातार fiat रहने का सबूत नहीं।
beats.on_screen: £ GBP; currency age ≠ fiat-regime age

beats.say: Euro अपनाने वाले EU members की एक समय गिनती 27 में 20 थी, बाकी 7 नहीं; सभी members नहीं। यह आज की updated गिनती नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Historical adoption count: 20 of 27 EU members; not a current count

beats.say: इन descriptions के numerical evidence नहीं हैं। Euro का ‘second-most’ अधूरा है; ranking का measure मत जोड़िए।
beats.on_screen: Qualitative captions; incomplete ranking remains incomplete

beats.say: Fiat worthless नहीं; reserves रखना gold redemption नहीं। Reserve currency भी fiat हो सकती है। Printing goods नहीं बनाती; policy demand सँभालेगी, हर supply shortage नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Value basis ≠ reserve use; more money ≠ more goods

beats.say: ₹100 उधार valid currency से चुकाएँ तो? ₹100 देने पर debt ₹100 से ₹0; यहाँ सवाल legally recognised settlement का है।
beats.on_screen: Recognised ₹100 payment: debt ₹100 → ₹0

beats.say: खास design वाला valid ₹10 coin मिले तो? ₹10 खरीद में दें: coins 1 से 0, unpaid amount ₹10 से ₹0; payment denomination पर हुई।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative special-design ₹10 coin → ₹10 purchase

beats.say: Bill ₹1,000 से ₹1,500 हो तो 2 की जगह 3 valid ₹500 notes दें; amount बढ़ा, tender ceiling नहीं आई। लेकिन ₹10 coins 100 से 101 हों, तो ₹1,000 से ₹1,010 होगा; extra coin लेना सामने वाले की मर्ज़ी है।
beats.on_screen: Notes: 2 → 3 without tender ceiling; coins: 100 → 101 crosses ₹1,000 ceiling

beats.say: Legal tender यानी territory में debts और transactions चुकाने के लिए government से officially recognised money। Circulation commemorative coins याद में बने coins हैं, जो रोज़ के payments में ordinary coins जैसे चलते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Legal recognition; circulation use despite special design

beats.say: Unlimited Legal Tender यानी genuine, valid notes जोड़ते जाएँ, coin जैसी total ceiling नहीं। ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100, ₹200, ₹500 notes का यह status Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 से जुड़ा है।
beats.on_screen: Valid notes stack without a tender-amount ceiling; RBI Act, 1934

beats.say: Limited Legal Tender में तय amount तक लेना ज़रूरी, आगे मर्ज़ी है; coins के लिए Coinage Act, 2011 है। इससे बहुत भारी coin payment लेने की कानूनी ज़रूरत नहीं रहती।
beats.on_screen: Prescribed ceiling → voluntary acceptance beyond; Coinage Act, 2011

beats.say: Unlimited हर cash transaction की छूट या नई sale का अधिकार नहीं। Voluntary acceptance legal status नहीं; valid coins की ceiling पार करना demonetization नहीं।
beats.on_screen: No universal retail compulsion; excess amount ≠ lost status

beats.say: पहले recognition, फिर notes की no-ceiling या coins की amount-limit जाँचिए।
beats.on_screen: Recognition → validity → ceiling

beats.say: क्या हर legal tender fiat ही होगा? सामान्य जोड़ ऐसा है, लेकिन universal ‘must’ गलत होगा; Bitcoin exception इसे तोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Fiat: value basis; legal tender: legal status

beats.say: याद में बना हर coin payment में चलेगा? Commemorative coins fiat issues हैं, लेकिन legal tender हो भी सकते हैं, नहीं भी; अधिकांश होने का मतलब सभी नहीं। Metal और collector value भी अलग रह सकती हैं।
beats.on_screen: Commemorative purpose ≠ automatic legal-tender status

beats.say: Pack वाला खास coin खर्च क्यों नहीं होता? Government Mint collector commemorative coins proof या UNC sets में बेचती है। Proof खास finish, UNC यानी Uncirculated; condition बचाने के लिए daily payments कम होते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Government Mint proof / UNC sets → collection rather than change drawer

beats.say: ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10, ₹20 coins की कुल limit ₹1,000 है, जैसे 50 coins ₹20 के। 50 paise का ढेर सिर्फ ₹10 तक; नीचे वाले coins payment money नहीं रहे।
beats.on_screen: Denomination groups → aggregate limits; ₹20 × 50 = ₹1,000

beats.say: 50 coins × ₹20 = ₹1,000; 1,000 coins की छूट नहीं। 50 paise के 20 coins = ₹10; denomination और total limit अलग हैं।
4 पुराने 25 paise coins से ₹1 bill चुकाएँ, दुकानदार मना करे तो ₹1 बाकी। Valid ₹1 coin दें तो ₹0; पुराने coins का legal-tender status हटना demonetization है।
beats.on_screen: Rejected old coins: ₹1 → ₹1; valid coin: ₹1 → ₹0

beats.say: Coinage Act, 2011 वाले limits में 50 paise अलग है; डिब्बे का 25 paise उसमें नहीं आता। Commemorative coins के लिए ‘most’ यानी सभी नहीं; इससे कोई गिनती नहीं मिलती।
beats.on_screen: 50 paise has its own limit; 25 paise is below that denomination; 'most' supplies no count

beats.say: Limit पार करना status खोना नहीं; collector price legal status लौटाती नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Excess amount ≠ demonetization

beats.say: Denomination × count निकालिए; फिर total limit और status जाँचिए।
beats.on_screen: Total = denomination × count → ceiling + status

beats.say: Phone पर Bitcoin payment दिखे तो government-issued money है? नहीं; El-Salvador का example issuance और legal status अलग करता है।
beats.on_screen: Network issuance ≠ government issuance

beats.say: 2024 तक का account Bitcoin को non-fiat legal-tender exception दिखाता है। Mining network rules से होती है; price demand-supply से, government के fixed-value promise से नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Dated account: non-fiat + legal recognition; network rules and market price

beats.say: 2025 reforms के बाद practical compulsory acceptance हटी; यानी दोनों राज़ी हों तो payment कर सकते हैं, लेना ज़रूरी नहीं। Ownership और voluntary use legal हैं—ban नहीं।
beats.on_screen: 2025 practical account: optional payment remains; compulsion removed

beats.say: Recognition से network issuance सरकारी नहीं बनती; यह पूरा statutory account भी नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Changed legal recognition ≠ changed issuer

beats.say: अलग पूछिए: issuer कौन, ownership legal, acceptance voluntary या compulsory?
beats.on_screen: Issuer | ownership | acceptance

beats.say: ₹100 silver commemorative coin पर collector कई हज़ार क्यों दे? वही coin payment और collection में अलग role निभाता है।
beats.on_screen: One coin: payment versus collector sale

beats.say: Payment में ₹100; collector sale में कई हज़ार संभव। Face value और market price अलग हैं।
beats.on_screen: ₹100 payment value | several-thousand collector price

beats.say: Silver, condition और collectability premium दिलाते हैं, denomination नहीं बदलते।
beats.on_screen: Collector premium ≠ new denomination

beats.say: Collector price debt-settlement amount या compulsory coin-payment limit नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Market price ≠ debt discharged ≠ tender ceiling

beats.say: Payment में denomination, collection में agreed price याद रखिए।
beats.on_screen: Payment: denomination | collection: agreed price

beats.say: ₹1,000 fees का cheque currency बन गया? Clearing हो तो student deposit ₹2,000 से ₹1,000, college ₹0 से ₹1,000। Funds कम हों तो transfer नहीं, fees बाकी।
beats.on_screen: Successful cheque clearing transfers existing deposits; failed clearing leaves fees due

beats.say: Alternative credit-card route में issuer arrangement से college को settlement मिलता है; charges छोड़कर student का card debt ₹0 से ₹1,000। यहाँ existing deposit का instruction नहीं, credit इस्तेमाल हुआ।
beats.on_screen: Alternative card route: student debt ₹0 → ₹1,000

beats.say: ये payment instruments हैं: cheque bank को instruction, card credit तक पहुँच। Accepted payment method होने से वे खुद fiat currency या legal tender नहीं बनते; fiat value का आधार है, legal tender कानूनी status।
beats.on_screen: Instrument ≠ currency; acceptance ≠ legal-tender status

beats.say: आखिरी trick: backing पूछे तो gold claim, value पूछे तो authority-trust, legal tender पूछे तो recognition और limits। Collector premium और payment instrument को इनसे अलग रखिए; आगे समझेंगे gold link टूटने पर भी dollar की माँग क्यों रही।
beats.on_screen: Backing | value basis | legal status | market price | payment method

problems.problem: The narration teaches the incompleteness of a source caption rather than the economics: “Euro का ‘second-most’ अधूरा है”. This still points at source material, despite the targeted correction to b29.
problems.fix: Teach the general boundary directly: a ranking requires a named measure and date; do not invent a euro ranking. Keep the source-caption limitation in production notes, not narration. Replace b30 rather than adding time.

problems.problem: Several milestones are date-label paraphrases rather than opened teaching. Yuan compulsory acceptance lacks its purpose and consequence; Britain’s gold standard lacks the need for a fixed anchor; Bretton Woods lacks why the dollar-gold link supplied an international reference. Their claimed explanations exceed what the beats actually teach.
problems.fix: Give each milestone a short need → arrangement → consequence explanation, distinguishing paper claims, state issuance, acceptance rules and monetary anchoring. Recover time from b5, b11, b18 and b22 rather than cutting historical content.

problems.problem: Currency captions are largely read out. “International reserves” is not opened through external-payment holdings, and b31 merely asserts that a reserve currency can be fiat. GBP’s source claim about being the oldest currency still in use is dropped rather than carefully qualified; the eighth-century date alone does not teach that distinction.
problems.fix: Explain reserve holdings with a country keeping foreign-currency assets for external payments, separating their use from gold backing. Preserve the pound’s long-continuity claim while explicitly separating currency age from the age of its fiat regime. Replace generic evidence commentary and repeated fiat recaps to make room.

problems.problem: The loss of legal-tender status for smaller coins is stated before its numerical example. This reverses the required economics example-first sequence, even though the word “demonetization” appears later.
problems.fix: Run the four rejected 25-paise coins and replacement ₹1 payment first, then name and define loss of legal-tender status and present the denomination table. Reorder existing narration without increasing length.

problems.problem: Repeated telegraphic fragments make portions sound like slide notes rather than complete spoken teaching: “notes 1 से 0”, “1275, Yuan: compulsory”, and “Mining network rules से होती है” are examples.
problems.fix: Use short complete Hinglish sentences describing actors and actions, especially in the timelines and numerical examples. Fund the extra connective words by removing duplicate recaps, not book facts.

problems.problem: The maker’s notes describe only a b29 patch, not the unit’s purpose, main teaching decisions or substantive uncertainties.
problems.fix: Replace patch-history notes with unit-level notes covering the three distinctions, treatment of overbroad source claims, historical date qualifications and unavailable evidence. This requires no narration time.

problems.problem: “Extra coin लेना ... मर्ज़ी” can suggest that compulsory acceptance of the first ₹1,000 remains enforceable within a single ₹1,010 offer. The safer teaching is that the offered total exceeds the tender ceiling.
problems.fix: Say that accepting a ₹1,010 coin payment is voluntary because the total offered exceeds ₹1,000. Replace the existing sentence.

replace_beats.say: एक hypothetical पुराने bank में note लौटाएँ तो क्या मिले? Bank 1 gram gold देता है; आपके notes 1 से 0 और gold 0 से 1 gram हो जाता है। आज का rupee ऐसा नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Historical illustration: holder returns 1 note and receives 1 gram gold; not today's rupee

replace_beats.say: Value gold claim से आई।
replace_beats.on_screen: Gold claim supports value

replace_beats.say: Bank के 10 grams से 10 notes के 1-gram claims पूरे होंगे। Fully backed उदाहरण में 11वाँ note जारी करे, तो gold 10 से 11 grams करना होगा।
replace_beats.on_screen: Illustrative full backing: 10 notes / 10 grams → 11 notes / 11 grams

replace_beats.say: Central bank gold रखकर notes जारी करता था और माँगने पर तय gold देता था। इसलिए नए notes को backing चाहिए थी; redemption in principle था, हर जगह unrestricted नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Reserves → note issue → fixed-gold redemption; in principle

replace_beats.say: Backing की ज़रूरत issue रोकती थी।
replace_beats.on_screen: Backing requirement constrains issue

replace_beats.say: जमा value का सबूत चाहिए तो receipt काम आती है; 7th century में Tang receipts यही paper-claim stage दिखाती हैं। 1023 के Song state notes में issuer सरकारी authority थी; अब पहचान सिर्फ claim की नहीं, जारी करने वाले की भी थी।
replace_beats.on_screen: 7th c. Tang: written claim → 1023 Song: state issuer

replace_beats.say: लोगों से पैसा स्वीकार करवाना हो तो नियम भी लगाया जा सकता है। 1275 का Yuan milestone compulsory acceptance दिखाता है: लेना सिर्फ मर्ज़ी नहीं रहा। Sweden के first banknotes 1661 में आए; इन्हें दुनिया के पहले मत समझिए, Chinese developments पहले हुए।
replace_beats.on_screen: 1275 Yuan: acceptance rule → 1661 Sweden: banknotes; earlier Chinese milestones remain visible

replace_beats.say: पैसे की इकाई को fixed आधार चाहिए था; Britain के 1816 Gold Standard ने उसे तय gold से जोड़ा। International exchange में common reference चाहिए था; 1944 Bretton Woods में dollar-gold link वह आधार बना। यह official convertibility थी, हर व्यक्ति का gold counter नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: 1816: monetary unit → fixed gold anchor; 1944: international reference → official dollar–gold link

replace_beats.say: 1971 में gold-redemption link टूटा; दोनों historical sequences यहीं modern fiat era तक पहुँचते हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Both historical sequences converge at 1971: no gold redemption

replace_beats.say: Claims से issuance, acceptance rules और anchors बदले।
replace_beats.on_screen: Full timeline: claims → state issue → acceptance rules → gold anchors → 1971 break

replace_beats.say: Fiat authority और trust से चलता है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Authority + public trust

replace_beats.say: ¥ Japan का है या China का? Japanese Yen का code JPY है; stability की पहचान वाला यह पैसा global currency markets में अहम है। Chinese Yuan Renminbi का code CNY है; trade और international reserves में इसकी भूमिका बढ़ी है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Shared symbol ¥; distinguish Japan / JPY from China / CNY

replace_beats.say: £ वाला British Pound Sterling, GBP, आज भी इस्तेमाल होने वाली सबसे पुरानी currency माना जाता है; इसकी जड़ें 8th century तक जाती हैं। आज यह fiat है, पर इतने पुराने समय से fiat था—यह निष्कर्ष गलत होगा; नाम चलता रह सकता है, backing बदल सकती है।
replace_beats.on_screen: GBP: long currency continuity since the 8th century ≠ continuous fiat regime

replace_beats.say: Ranking में measure और date चाहिए: holding या trading, और कब? Stability या बढ़ती भूमिका जैसे descriptions अपने-आप numerical proof नहीं हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Ranking test: measure + date + data; do not infer a euro ranking

replace_beats.say: देश बाहरी payments के लिए foreign-currency assets रखे, वे international reserves हैं; यह इस्तेमाल है, gold backing नहीं। Fiat worthless नहीं; gold रखना redemption नहीं। Printing goods नहीं बनाती; policy demand सँभाल सकती है, हर supply shortage नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Foreign-currency holdings → external payments; reserve use ≠ gold backing; money creation ≠ goods creation

replace_beats.say: 4 पुराने 25 paise coins दें तो ₹1 bill चुक जाएगा? दुकानदार मना करे तो ₹1 बाकी रहता है; valid ₹1 coin दें तो बकाया ₹0 होता है। पुराने coins का legal-tender status हटना demonetization है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Four old 25-paise coins refused: debt ₹1 → ₹1; valid ₹1 replacement: debt ₹1 → ₹0

replace_beats.say: कितने coins दे सकते हैं? ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10, ₹20 coins की total limit ₹1,000 है। 50 paise coins की limit ₹10 है; 50 paise से नीचे के coins legal tender नहीं रहे।
replace_beats.on_screen: Coin denomination → aggregate tender limit: listed rupee coins ₹1,000; 50 paise ₹10; below 50 paise no legal-tender status

replace_beats.say: ₹20 के 50 coins जोड़ें तो ₹1,000 बनते हैं; limit 1,000 coins की नहीं है। 50 paise के 20 coins जोड़ें तो ₹10 बनते हैं; denomination और total limit अलग हैं।

2024 तक El-Salvador में Bitcoin non-fiat legal-tender exception था। Miners network के rules के तहत नए bitcoin बनाते हैं; buyers और sellers की demand-supply price तय करती है, government fixed value का वादा नहीं करती।

beats.say: ₹100 note का कागज़ सस्ता है, फिर भी चावल मिलते हैं—क्या पीछे gold रखा होना ज़रूरी है? और payment में कोई चीज़ ले ली जाए, तो क्या वह legal tender बन जाती है?
beats.on_screen: ₹100 note → rice; gold backing? Legal status?

beats.say: एक hypothetical पुराने bank में note लौटाएँ तो क्या मिले? Bank 1 gram gold देता है; आपके notes 1 से 0 और gold 0 से 1 gram हो जाता है। आज का rupee ऐसा नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Historical illustration: holder returns 1 note and receives 1 gram gold; not today's rupee

beats.say: यह gold-backed paper currency है: माँगने पर तय gold मिले। Intrinsic value यानी material की कीमत; यहाँ value paper से नहीं, redemption promise से है, जैसे सामान की receipt।
beats.on_screen: Paper material ≠ redeemable gold claim

beats.say: सिर्फ bank का gold रखना काफी नहीं; note लौटाने पर gold मिलना चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Gold assets alone ≠ redeemability

beats.say: Value gold claim से आई।
beats.on_screen: Gold claim supports value

beats.say: Bank के 10 grams से 10 notes के 1-gram claims पूरे होंगे। Fully backed उदाहरण में 11वाँ note जारी करे, तो gold 10 से 11 grams करना होगा।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative full backing: 10 notes / 10 grams → 11 notes / 11 grams

beats.say: यही gold-backing constraint है; gold reserves यानी claims पूरे करने का stock।
beats.on_screen: Reserves support redemption claims

beats.say: Central bank gold रखकर notes जारी करता था और माँगने पर तय gold देता था। इसलिए नए notes को backing चाहिए थी; redemption in principle था, हर जगह unrestricted नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Reserves → note issue → fixed-gold redemption; in principle

beats.say: Claims चुकाने की क्षमता घटे, तो भरोसा टूटे और लोग gold माँगें।
beats.on_screen: Unmeetable claims → redemption pressure

beats.say: हर note पर 1 gram सिर्फ उदाहरण है, historical reserve ratio नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Illustration, not a historical reserve ratio

beats.say: Backing की ज़रूरत issue रोकती थी।
beats.on_screen: Backing requirement constrains issue

beats.say: सामान की जगह receipt चले तो? इतिहास में paper claims, सरकारी issue और acceptance rules अलग milestones बने।
beats.on_screen: Paper claim → state issue → acceptance rules

beats.say: जमा value का सबूत चाहिए तो receipt काम आती है; 7th century में Tang receipts यही paper-claim stage दिखाती हैं। 1023 के Song state notes में issuer सरकारी authority थी; अब पहचान सिर्फ claim की नहीं, जारी करने वाले की भी थी।
beats.on_screen: 7th c. Tang: written claim → 1023 Song: state issuer

beats.say: लोगों से पैसा स्वीकार करवाना हो तो नियम भी लगाया जा सकता है। 1275 का Yuan milestone compulsory acceptance दिखाता है: लेना सिर्फ मर्ज़ी नहीं रहा। Sweden के first banknotes 1661 में आए; इन्हें दुनिया के पहले मत समझिए, Chinese developments पहले हुए।
beats.on_screen: 1275 Yuan: acceptance rule → 1661 Sweden: banknotes; earlier Chinese milestones remain visible

beats.say: पैसे की इकाई को fixed आधार चाहिए था; Britain के 1816 Gold Standard ने उसे तय gold से जोड़ा। International exchange में common reference चाहिए था; 1944 Bretton Woods में dollar-gold link वह आधार बना। यह official convertibility थी, हर व्यक्ति का gold counter नहीं।
beats.on_screen: 1816: monetary unit → fixed gold anchor; 1944: international reference → official dollar–gold link

beats.say: 1971 में gold-redemption link टूटा; दोनों historical sequences यहीं modern fiat era तक पहुँचते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Both historical sequences converge at 1971: no gold redemption

beats.say: अब gold promise की जगह authority और trust से value समझेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Gold promise → authority and trust

beats.say: Claims से issuance, acceptance rules और anchors बदले।
beats.on_screen: Full timeline: claims → state issue → acceptance rules → gold anchors → 1971 break

beats.say: दुकानदार ₹100 note लेकर चावल क्यों दे? खरीदने पर आपकी cash ₹100 से ₹0, उसकी receipt ₹0 से ₹100; भरोसा है, आगे वही note चलेगा।
beats.on_screen: Buyer ₹100 → ₹0; seller ₹0 → ₹100 → next purchase

beats.say: यह fiat money है: value government authority और public trust से, material से नहीं। यानी आज मिला note कल groceries दिलाएगा।
beats.on_screen: Authority + continued acceptance, not material value

beats.say: Gold-backed paper का आधार redemption था; इसलिए हर paper note fiat नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Paper form ≠ fiat basis

beats.say: Fiat authority और trust से चलता है।
beats.on_screen: Authority + public trust

beats.say: Press से note निकलना और पैसा जारी होना क्या एक काम है? Fiat paper या digital numbers हो सकता है; face value gold-silver से नहीं बँधी, government authority, central-bank control और public trust से जुड़ी है।
beats.on_screen: Material value; commodity backing; authority; trust

beats.say: और issue कर सकते हैं, मगर monetary policy control करती है। Printing notes बनाती है; authorised issuance circulation में लाता है। पुराने notes बदलना कुल पैसा बढ़ाना नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Printing ≠ issuance; replacement need not increase currency

beats.say: RBI banknotes जारी करता है; ₹1 note और coins government, coins distribution RBI करता है। Policy rates और liquidity से borrowing महँगी-सस्ती होती है; spending और prices तक असर समय लेता है।
beats.on_screen: Issuer distinctions; policy → borrowing → spending → prices

beats.say: Foreign price tags में codes क्यों देखें? $ वाला United States Dollar, USD, सबसे widely held और traded fiat currency है। € यानी Euro, EUR, कई EU देशों की shared currency है।
beats.on_screen: $ USD: United States Dollar; € EUR: Euro

beats.say: ¥ Japan का है या China का? Japanese Yen का code JPY है; stability की पहचान वाला यह पैसा global currency markets में अहम है। Chinese Yuan Renminbi का code CNY है; trade और international reserves में इसकी भूमिका बढ़ी है।
beats.on_screen: Shared symbol ¥; distinguish Japan / JPY from China / CNY

beats.say: £ वाला British Pound Sterling, GBP, आज भी इस्तेमाल होने वाली सबसे पुरानी currency माना जाता है; इसकी जड़ें 8th century तक जाती हैं। आज यह fiat है, पर इतने पुराने समय से fiat था—यह निष्कर्ष गलत होगा; नाम चलता रह सकता है, backing बदल सकती है।
beats.on_screen: GBP: long currency continuity since the 8th century ≠ continuous fiat regime

beats.say: Euro अपनाने वाले EU members की एक समय गिनती 27 में 20 थी, बाकी 7 नहीं; सभी members नहीं। यह आज की updated गिनती नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Historical adoption count: 20 of 27 EU members; not a current count

beats.say: Ranking में measure और date चाहिए: holding या trading, और कब? Stability या बढ़ती भूमिका जैसे descriptions अपने-आप numerical proof नहीं हैं।
beats.on_screen: Ranking test: measure + date + data; do not infer a euro ranking

beats.say: देश बाहरी payments के लिए foreign-currency assets रखे, वे international reserves हैं; यह इस्तेमाल है, gold backing नहीं। Fiat worthless नहीं; gold रखना redemption नहीं। Printing goods नहीं बनाती; policy demand सँभाल सकती है, हर supply shortage नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Foreign-currency holdings → external payments; reserve use ≠ gold backing; money creation ≠ goods creation

beats.say: ₹100 उधार valid currency से चुकाएँ तो? ₹100 देने पर debt ₹100 से ₹0; यहाँ सवाल legally recognised settlement का है।
beats.on_screen: Recognised ₹100 payment: debt ₹100 → ₹0

beats.say: खास design वाला valid ₹10 coin मिले तो? ₹10 खरीद में दें: coins 1 से 0, unpaid amount ₹10 से ₹0; payment denomination पर हुई।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative special-design ₹10 coin → ₹10 purchase

beats.say: Bill ₹1,000 से ₹1,500 हो तो 2 की जगह 3 valid ₹500 notes दें; amount बढ़ा, tender ceiling नहीं आई। लेकिन ₹10 coins 100 से 101 हों, तो ₹1,000 से ₹1,010 होगा; extra coin लेना सामने वाले की मर्ज़ी है।
beats.on_screen: Notes: 2 → 3 without tender ceiling; coins: 100 → 101 crosses ₹1,000 ceiling

beats.say: Legal tender यानी territory में debts और transactions चुकाने के लिए government से officially recognised money। Circulation commemorative coins याद में बने coins हैं, जो रोज़ के payments में ordinary coins जैसे चलते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Legal recognition; circulation use despite special design

beats.say: Unlimited Legal Tender यानी genuine, valid notes जोड़ते जाएँ, coin जैसी total ceiling नहीं। ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100, ₹200, ₹500 notes का यह status Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 से जुड़ा है।
beats.on_screen: Valid notes stack without a tender-amount ceiling; RBI Act, 1934

beats.say: Limited Legal Tender में तय amount तक लेना ज़रूरी, आगे मर्ज़ी है; coins के लिए Coinage Act, 2011 है। इससे बहुत भारी coin payment लेने की कानूनी ज़रूरत नहीं रहती।
beats.on_screen: Prescribed ceiling → voluntary acceptance beyond; Coinage Act, 2011

beats.say: Unlimited हर cash transaction की छूट या नई sale का अधिकार नहीं। Voluntary acceptance legal status नहीं; valid coins की ceiling पार करना demonetization नहीं।
beats.on_screen: No universal retail compulsion; excess amount ≠ lost status

beats.say: पहले recognition, फिर notes की no-ceiling या coins की amount-limit जाँचिए।
beats.on_screen: Recognition → validity → ceiling

beats.say: क्या हर legal tender fiat ही होगा? सामान्य जोड़ ऐसा है, लेकिन universal ‘must’ गलत होगा; Bitcoin exception इसे तोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Fiat: value basis; legal tender: legal status

beats.say: याद में बना हर coin payment में चलेगा? Commemorative coins fiat issues हैं, लेकिन legal tender हो भी सकते हैं, नहीं भी; अधिकांश होने का मतलब सभी नहीं। Metal और collector value भी अलग रह सकती हैं।
beats.on_screen: Commemorative purpose ≠ automatic legal-tender status

beats.say: Pack वाला खास coin खर्च क्यों नहीं होता? Government Mint collector commemorative coins proof या UNC sets में बेचती है। Proof खास finish, UNC यानी Uncirculated; condition बचाने के लिए daily payments कम होते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Government Mint proof / UNC sets → collection rather than change drawer

beats.say: 4 पुराने 25 paise coins दें तो ₹1 bill चुक जाएगा? दुकानदार मना करे तो ₹1 बाकी रहता है; valid ₹1 coin दें तो बकाया ₹0 होता है। पुराने coins का legal-tender status हटना demonetization है।
beats.on_screen: Four old 25-paise coins refused: debt ₹1 → ₹1; valid ₹1 replacement: debt ₹1 → ₹0

beats.say: कितने coins दे सकते हैं? ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10, ₹20 coins की total limit ₹1,000 है। 50 paise coins की limit ₹10 है; 50 paise से नीचे के coins legal tender नहीं रहे।
beats.on_screen: Coin denomination → aggregate tender limit: listed rupee coins ₹1,000; 50 paise ₹10; below 50 paise no legal-tender status

beats.say: ₹20 के 50 coins जोड़ें तो ₹1,000 बनते हैं; limit 1,000 coins की नहीं है। 50 paise के 20 coins जोड़ें तो ₹10 बनते हैं; denomination और total limit अलग हैं।
Coinage Act, 2011 वाले limits में 50 paise अलग है; डिब्बे का 25 paise उसमें नहीं आता। Commemorative coins के लिए ‘most’ यानी सभी नहीं; इससे कोई गिनती नहीं मिलती।
beats.on_screen: 50 paise has its own limit; 25 paise is below that denomination; 'most' supplies no count

beats.say: Limit पार करना status खोना नहीं; collector price legal status लौटाती नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Excess amount ≠ demonetization

beats.say: Denomination × count निकालिए; फिर total limit और status जाँचिए।
beats.on_screen: Total = denomination × count → ceiling + status

beats.say: Phone पर Bitcoin payment दिखे तो government-issued money है? नहीं; El-Salvador का example issuance और legal status अलग करता है।
beats.on_screen: Network issuance ≠ government issuance

beats.say: 2024 तक El-Salvador में Bitcoin non-fiat legal-tender exception था। Miners network के rules के तहत नए bitcoin बनाते हैं; buyers और sellers की demand-supply price तय करती है, government fixed value का वादा नहीं करती।
beats.on_screen: Dated historical status through 2024; network-governed issuance; market price, not sovereign fixed-value promise

beats.say: 2025 reforms के बाद practical compulsory acceptance हटी; यानी दोनों राज़ी हों तो payment कर सकते हैं, लेना ज़रूरी नहीं। Ownership और voluntary use legal हैं—ban नहीं।
beats.on_screen: 2025 practical account: optional payment remains; compulsion removed

beats.say: Recognition से network issuance सरकारी नहीं बनती; यह पूरा statutory account भी नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Changed legal recognition ≠ changed issuer

beats.say: अलग पूछिए: issuer कौन, ownership legal, acceptance voluntary या compulsory?
beats.on_screen: Issuer | ownership | acceptance

beats.say: ₹100 silver commemorative coin पर collector कई हज़ार क्यों दे? वही coin payment और collection में अलग role निभाता है।
beats.on_screen: One coin: payment versus collector sale

beats.say: Payment में ₹100; collector sale में कई हज़ार संभव। Face value और market price अलग हैं।
beats.on_screen: ₹100 payment value | several-thousand collector price

beats.say: Collector silver, condition और collectability के लिए ज़्यादा देता है; denomination नहीं बदलती।
beats.on_screen: Silver + condition + collectability → premium; face value remains ₹100

beats.say: Collector price debt-settlement amount या compulsory coin-payment limit नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Market price ≠ debt discharged ≠ tender ceiling

beats.say: Payment में denomination, collection में agreed price याद रखिए।
beats.on_screen: Payment: denomination | collection: agreed price

beats.say: ₹1,000 fees का cheque currency बन गया? Clearing हो तो student deposit ₹2,000 से ₹1,000, college ₹0 से ₹1,000। Funds कम हों तो transfer नहीं, fees बाकी।
beats.on_screen: Successful cheque clearing transfers existing deposits; failed clearing leaves fees due

beats.say: Alternative credit-card route में issuer arrangement से college को settlement मिलता है; charges छोड़कर student का card debt ₹0 से ₹1,000। यहाँ existing deposit का instruction नहीं, credit इस्तेमाल हुआ।
beats.on_screen: Alternative card route: student debt ₹0 → ₹1,000

beats.say: ये payment instruments हैं: cheque bank को instruction, card credit तक पहुँच। Accepted payment method होने से वे खुद fiat currency या legal tender नहीं बनते; fiat value का आधार है, legal tender कानूनी status।
beats.on_screen: Instrument ≠ currency; acceptance ≠ legal-tender status

beats.say: आखिरी trick: backing पूछे तो gold claim, value पूछे तो authority-trust, legal tender पूछे तो recognition और limits। Collector premium और payment instrument को इनसे अलग रखिए; आगे समझेंगे gold link टूटने पर भी dollar की माँग क्यों रही।
beats.on_screen: Backing | value basis | legal status | market price | payment method

beats.say: Legal tender यानी territory में debts और transactions चुकाने के लिए government से officially recognised money। Circulation commemorative coins याद में बने coins हैं, जो रोज़ के payments में ordinary coins जैसे चलते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Legal recognition; circulation use despite special design

beats.say: Unlimited Legal Tender में genuine, valid notes की total tender ceiling नहीं। ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100, ₹200, ₹500 notes को जोड़िए; यह status Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 से जुड़ा है।
beats.on_screen: Listed genuine, valid banknotes → no aggregate tender ceiling; RBI Act, 1934

beats.say: Limited Legal Tender में तय amount तक लेना ज़रूरी, आगे मर्ज़ी है; coins के लिए Coinage Act, 2011 है। इससे बहुत भारी coin payment लेने की कानूनी ज़रूरत नहीं रहती।
beats.on_screen: Prescribed ceiling → voluntary acceptance beyond; Coinage Act, 2011

beats.say: Unlimited हर cash transaction की छूट या नई sale का अधिकार नहीं। Voluntary acceptance legal status नहीं; valid coins की ceiling पार करना demonetization नहीं।
beats.on_screen: No universal retail compulsion; excess amount ≠ lost status

beats.say: पहले recognition, फिर notes की no-ceiling या coins की amount-limit जाँचिए।
beats.on_screen: Recognition → validity → ceiling

beats.say: क्या हर legal tender fiat ही होगा? सामान्य जोड़ ऐसा है, लेकिन universal ‘must’ गलत होगा; Bitcoin exception इसे तोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Fiat: value basis; legal tender: legal status

beats.say: याद में बना हर coin payment में चलेगा? Commemorative coins fiat issues हैं, लेकिन legal tender हो भी सकते हैं, नहीं भी; अधिकांश होने का मतलब सभी नहीं। Metal और collector value भी अलग रह सकती हैं।
beats.on_screen: Commemorative purpose ≠ automatic legal-tender status

beats.say: Pack वाला coin खर्च क्यों नहीं होता? Government Mint collector commemorative coins proof या UNC sets में बेचती है। Proof खास finish, UNC यानी Uncirculated; condition बचाने के लिए daily payments कम होते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Government Mint collector sets: proof finish / uncirculated condition → preservation

beats.say: 4 पुराने 25 paise coins दें तो ₹1 bill चुक जाएगा? दुकानदार मना करे तो ₹1 बाकी रहता है; valid ₹1 coin दें तो बकाया ₹0 होता है। पुराने coins का legal-tender status हटना demonetization है।
beats.on_screen: Four old 25-paise coins refused: debt ₹1 → ₹1; valid ₹1 replacement: debt ₹1 → ₹0

beats.say: Change के डिब्बे में कौन-से coins हैं? ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10, ₹20 को जोड़कर ₹1,000 तक की tender limit है। 50 paise जोड़ें तो ₹10 तक; उससे छोटे coins जोड़ने से legal-tender payment नहीं बनता।
beats.on_screen: Sort change drawer: listed rupee coins → ₹1,000 meter; 50 paise → ₹10 meter; smaller coins → no tender status

beats.say: ₹20 के 50 coins जोड़ें तो ₹1,000 बनते हैं; limit 1,000 coins की नहीं है। 50 paise के 20 coins जोड़ें तो ₹10 बनते हैं; denomination और total limit अलग हैं।
Coinage Act, 2011 के limits में 50 paise की अलग जगह है, 25 paise की नहीं। Commemorative coins में ‘most’ कोई numerical count नहीं देता।
beats.on_screen: 50 paise ≠ below 50 paise; 'most' supplies no numerical count

beats.say: Limit पार करना status खोना नहीं; collector price legal status लौटाती नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Excess amount ≠ demonetization

beats.say: Denomination × count निकालिए; फिर total limit और status जाँचिए।
beats.on_screen: Total = denomination × count → ceiling + status

beats.say: Phone पर Bitcoin payment दिखे तो government-issued money है? नहीं; El-Salvador का example issuance और legal status अलग करता है।
beats.on_screen: Network issuance ≠ government issuance

beats.say: 2024 तक El-Salvador में Bitcoin non-fiat legal-tender exception था। नए bitcoin mining से network rules के मुताबिक बनते हैं; price buyers-sellers की demand-supply से, government के fixed-value promise से नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Dated account through 2024; mining under network rules; market price rather than sovereign fixed-value promise

beats.say: 2025 reforms के बाद practical compulsory acceptance हटी; ownership और voluntary use legal रहे। दोनों राज़ी हों तो payment संभव है—यह ban नहीं।
beats.on_screen: 2025 practical account: compulsion removed; legal ownership and voluntary use remain

beats.say: Recognition से network issuance सरकारी नहीं बनती; यह पूरा statutory account भी नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Changed legal recognition ≠ changed issuer

beats.say: अलग पूछिए: issuer कौन, ownership legal, acceptance voluntary या compulsory?
beats.on_screen: Issuer | ownership | acceptance

beats.say: ₹100 silver commemorative coin पर collector कई हज़ार क्यों दे? वही coin payment और collection में अलग role निभाता है।
beats.on_screen: One coin: payment versus collector sale

beats.say: Payment में ₹100; collector sale में कई हज़ार संभव। Face value और market price अलग हैं।
beats.on_screen: ₹100 payment value | several-thousand collector price

beats.say: Collector silver, condition और collectability के लिए ज़्यादा देता है; denomination नहीं बदलती।
beats.on_screen: Silver + condition + collectability → premium; face value remains ₹100

beats.say: Collector price debt-settlement amount या compulsory coin-payment limit नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Market price ≠ debt discharged ≠ tender ceiling

beats.say: Payment में denomination, collection में agreed price याद रखिए।
beats.on_screen: Payment: denomination | collection: agreed price

beats.say: ₹1,000 fees का cheque currency बन गया? Clearing हो तो student deposit ₹2,000 से ₹1,000, college ₹0 से ₹1,000। Funds कम हों तो transfer नहीं, fees बाकी।
beats.on_screen: Successful cheque clearing transfers existing deposits; failed clearing leaves fees due

beats.say: Alternative credit-card route में issuer arrangement से college को settlement मिलता है; charges छोड़कर student का card debt ₹0 से ₹1,000। यहाँ existing deposit का instruction नहीं, credit इस्तेमाल हुआ।
beats.on_screen: Alternative card route: student debt ₹0 → ₹1,000

beats.say: ये payment instruments हैं: cheque bank को instruction, card credit तक पहुँच। Accepted payment method होने से वे खुद fiat currency या legal tender नहीं बनते; fiat value का आधार है, legal tender कानूनी status।
beats.on_screen: Instrument ≠ currency; acceptance ≠ legal-tender status

beats.say: Gold claim, authority-trust और legal recognition अलग सवाल हैं। Limits, collector premium और payment instruments भी अलग रखिए। आगे: gold link टूटकर भी dollar की माँग क्यों रही?
beats.on_screen: Backing | value basis | legal status | collector price | payment instrument
